Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Austin/San Antonio TX
541 AM CDT Sat Mar 14 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very windy with critical fire weather conditions, and much
  colder temperatures expected behind a strong cold front Sunday 
  afternoon into Sunday night

- Remains warm in the advance of the front with near record highs
  Sunday; returns to near record highs by the end of the workweek
  on Friday

- Dry forecast for the next 7 days outside of low (10-20%) chances
  across our eastern most coastal plain counties with the front's
  passage

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 1235 AM CDT Sat Mar 14 2026

Low-level moisture slowly but steadily advances inland overnight 
into this morning with the light southerly flow. Low stratus should 
develop and expand across the region as a result. Some pockets of 
patchy fog could develop across the Hill Country and San Antonio 
metro area but the stratus deck is more favored compared to any 
widespread fog formation. Expect these low clouds to erode by 
afternoon, resulting in a a mostly sunny afternoon featuring highs 
in the mid to upper 80s for the majority of the region. The Rio 
Grande will be the exception where highs could reach into the low 
90s. Moderate southerly winds trend through the afternoon with 
gustiness into the 20 to 25 mph range. Saturday night will trend 
warmer and more humid as the southerly low-level flow intensifies in 
response to a strengthening surface low-pressure system advancing 
across the Central Plains with connection to a sharp and digging 
upper level trough. Low clouds will return with a pocket or two of 
patchy fog into Sunday morning.

Sunday through Sunday night is the most impactful weather over the 
next week. Initially, expect a dryline to gradually mix eastward 
towards the highway 281 corridor. This will quickly erode any low 
clouds out west that morning and should setup for near record heat 
across the region. The highest temperatures occur in the dry and 
westerly flow behind the dryline. Highs are to reach the mid to 
upper 90s along the Rio Grande. A location or two could even reach 
100 degrees. Temperatures will be hot elsewhere as well with the 
highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. This is when the threat for 
critical fire weather conditions is set to begin due to the dry air 
and enough pre-frontal wind. The critical fire weather conditions 
will become prolonged with the arrival of a strong cold front, 
please see the details below.

A powerful cold front in association with the strong surface low 
moving across the Midwest arrives from the north during the latter 
half of Sunday afternoon through Sunday evening. The front should 
remain primarily rain free but there may be the slight chance a 
narrow band of showers and/or a storm develops across our eastern 
most counties, mainly over Fayette and Lavaca counties. The front 
will otherwise bring very strong winds immediately on the boundary 
and in it's wake from the north. A Wind Advisory will nearly be a 
slam dunk with sustained winds into the 20 to 35 mph range with 
higher gusts of 45 to 55 mph. This strong northerly flow would 
advect much colder air into the region as well. Temperatures into 
Monday morning will fall into the 30s and low 40s with wind chills 
as low as the 20s and low to mid 30s. A light freeze could even 
develop despite the elevated wind speeds for portions of the Hill 
Country and Southern Edwards Plateau. Despite the cold air, the 
humidity recovery will only remain modest overnight, and would 
prolong concerns for critical fire weather conditions with the 
winds. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 1235 AM CDT Sat Mar 14 2026

Monday will be unseasonably cool with the highs staying mainly in 
the 50s to low 60s. There could also be an increase in clouds as 
well with an increase in wind energy along the base of the main 
trough. A breezy northerly flow maintains through the day but will 
not be nearly as strong as the winds Sunday night. However, the 
winds remain enough with the low humidity for a continued concern 
for potential critical fire weather conditions. The winds weaken 
into Monday night with surface high pressure settling across the 
state. This results in an efficient night for radiational cooling 
where most locations see colder temperatures into Tuesday morning 
compared to Monday morning. This could allow for a light freeze 
through the Hill Country, but also into portions of the I-35 
Corridor and Coastal Plains. 

The rest of the week will see a strong mid-level ridge develop in 
the western CONUS while troughing remains most settled along the 
CONUS east coast. That ridging to our west starts to expand and 
slowly inch eastward towards the region. This and a return of the 
southerly low-level winds across the region lead into a warming 
trend from mid to late week. Afternoon highs from Friday into 
Saturday may actually start to threaten daily record highs once 
more. Conditions remain rain free under mostly clear to partly 
cloudy skies.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 541 AM CDT Sat Mar 14 2026

Shallow low level moisture has made it to the I-35 corridor and will 
linger through mid morning with areas of IFR/MVFR CIGs. Then, VFR is 
expected remainder of today through this evening. MVFR CIGs return 
to most areas overnight into Sunday morning. Southerly winds 
increase to 10 to 15 KTs by midday and prevail through early Sunday. 
Gusts to around 25 KTs are possible mainly this afternoon into early 
evening. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1235 AM CDT Sat Mar 14 2026

Prolonged stretch of critical fire weather conditions expected on 
Sunday through Monday with combination of a dryline followed by a 
strong cold front. A Fire Weather Watch has been issued for the 
entirety of South-Central Texas starting Noon Sunday and will 
continue through 8 PM on Monday evening. Following the dryline on 
Sunday, west winds of 10 to 20 mph with higher gusts develop and 
humidity levels will fall into the 10 to 25 percent range with 
afternoon temperatures in the 90s for most. The dryline then gets 
overtaken by a strong cold front from the second half of Sunday 
afternoon through Sunday evening. Very strong north winds will 
arrive immediately and in wake of this front with sustained wind 
speeds in the 20 to 35 mph range and gusts up to 45 to 55 mph. 
Expect for these strong winds to persist during the overnight and 
despite the rapidly falling temperatures, moisture recovery will 
remain poor with highest humidity only in the 25 to 35 percent 
range. Winds will remain breezy through Monday afternoon but will 
not be quite as strong as the speeds overnight. However, expect 
minimum humidity to fall back into the 10 to 20 percent range on 
Monday afternoon. Speeds finally weaken to light levels during 
Monday night. Dry conditions persist through midweek with perhaps 
enough wind at times for elevated fire weather conditions across 
portions of the region. Humidity levels gradually recover late this 
week with the return and increase in southerly flow.
